senses.definition: An instant response made without thinking, often driven by habit or strong feeling.
senses.caution: It says the response was not thought through. About your own first response it sounds honest, but about someone else's it can sound dismissive.
senses.example: Banning all AI tools after one leak was a knee-jerk reaction, so let us look at what actually went wrong.

cues.text: After one bad customer review, a director wants to rewrite the whole sign-up flow by Friday, and you ask the team to wait for more data.
A single outage leads someone to propose banning all Friday deploys forever, before anyone has found the cause.
In a retro you admit that blaming the vendor for the audit finding came before you had read the report.
A friend sells all their shares the morning prices drop, without checking why they fell.

distractors: A formal complaint sent to a manager.
A decision made only after a long review of the evidence.
A reply that is delayed on purpose so that it seems more thoughtful.
A plan written down in advance for what to do if a known risk actually happens during a project.
A change agreed by every team that it affects, after they have all had time to read it and comment.
